newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end lower on stocks' rebound.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end lower on stocks' rebound.

text.p: The key September Euroyen futures contract ended Wednesday's TIFFE day session lower after a fall in Japanese government bonds (JGBs) and the strong rebound in Tokyo stocks.
September closed at an intraday low of 99.27. Volume was 20,616 contracts.
"Euroyen futures fell due to Tokyo stocks' rebound and JGBs' weakness," said a city bank trader.
The key Nikkei 225 average ended up 387.70 points or 2.02 percent at 19,549.41, after falling 529 points or 2.69 percent on Tuesday.
Meanwhile, key March JGB futures closed down 0.30 at 125.30.
A weak stock market is seen supportive for Euroyen futures as it underscores the need for the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to maintain an easy credit policy, traders said.
Traders said payments by some banks in the interest rate swap (IRS) market was partly responsible today's selling in the Euroyen futures market.
"The September contract is likely to trade between the 20-day moving average of around 99.20/21 and the recent high of 99.33 (set on Friday) for the time being," a trust bank trader said.
Trading was curtailed due to the Christmas holiday in overseas markets, traders said.
In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.50 percent, up from 0.49 percent on Tuesday.
The BOJ drained a net 300 billion yen from the money market in the morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
About 270 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.52 percent, the highest level since November 13, traders said.
Three-month CDs were offered at 0.51 percent on the previous day.
Today's rise in three-month CD rates was due to increased fund demand ahead of the year-end, traders said.
